title: Fraud Detection: 3+ Transactions Within 1 Hour
description:
A `transactions` table records customer purchases with timestamps. **Detect potentially fraudulent customers** who made 3 or more transactions within any rolling 1-hour window. Return the customer_id and the maximum number of transactions found in any single 1-hour window for that customer.

**Table: transactions**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| txn_id | INT |
| customer_id | INT |
| txn_time | TIMESTAMP |
| amount | NUMERIC(10,2) |
| merchant_id | INT |

Output columns: `customer_id`, `max_txns_in_1hr`. Order by `customer_id`.
solution_sql: WITH window_counts AS (SELECT t1.customer_id, t1.txn_id, COUNT(*) AS txns_in_window FROM transactions t1 JOIN transactions t2 ON t1.customer_id = t2.customer_id AND t2.txn_time >= t1.txn_time AND t2.txn_time < t1.txn_time + INTERVAL '1 hour' GROUP BY t1.customer_id, t1.txn_id) SELECT customer_id, MAX(txns_in_window) AS max_txns_in_1hr FROM window_counts GROUP BY customer_id HAVING MAX(txns_in_window) >= 3 ORDER BY customer_id

test_cases.description: Customers with 3+ transactions in any 1-hour window

hints: Self-join the transactions table on customer_id, anchoring on each transaction t1 and counting all t2 transactions where t2.txn_time falls within [t1.txn_time, t1.txn_time + 1 hour). This gives the count of transactions in the 1-hour window starting at each transaction.

The outer query groups by customer_id and applies HAVING MAX(txns_in_window) >= 3 to keep only customers where at least one window had 3 or more transactions. Customer 102 has a 70-minute gap between its only two transactions and is correctly excluded.
explanation: For each anchor transaction t1, a self-join counts all transactions t2 from the same customer that occur within the next 60 minutes. Customer 101's window starting at 10:00 covers transactions at 10:00, 10:20, and 10:45 (3 in 45 minutes). Customer 103's window starting at 09:00 covers 09:00, 09:30, and 09:55 (3 in 55 minutes), and a second window at 09:30 also covers 3 (09:30, 09:55, 10:15). Customer 102's only pair is 70 minutes apart, so no window hits the threshold. The HAVING clause efficiently filters to only the flagged customers. This pattern is a core component of real-time fraud scoring at payment processors.
